## Ontology terms

| term | definition | notes |
|---|---|---|
| containment policy | The typed, provenance-bearing, content-addressed data document `ContainmentPolicy/1{fs, net, proc, resources, amendment, residual_channels, ext}` attached to an environment handle that bounds what processes inside the environment can read/write/execute, reach on the network, become (privilege/namespaces) and consume. Data, never code. | WS-H4 / WS-B5. Codex `SandboxPolicy`/`PermissionProfile`, sandbox-runtime schemas, Harbor `NetworkPolicy` as partial precedents. |
| containment floor / capability ceiling | The precedence rule of `authorize(p)`: `allow` requires both that the effective containment policy *admits* the effect (floor — enforced below the model regardless of the monitor's verdict) and that a valid `Permission` *covers* it (ceiling — authority the monitor may confer). Neither loosens the other. | WS-H4 / WS-H1. Doc 2 §5.6 "deterministic containment is the backstop". |
| effective containment policy | `effective(layers[])`: the authority-ordered meet of policy layers in which deny wins, booleans AND, allow sets intersect across lower-authority layers, and only `principal`/`definition` layers may loosen designated fields; sealed into the run manifest. | WS-H4. Codex `EnvironmentNetworkPolicy.apply_to`; ADR-0024/0034 layering. |
| enforcement point | One of E1 machine boundary (namespaces / user-space kernel / microVM), E2 process sandbox helper (Seatbelt / bubblewrap + seccomp / Landlock / restricted token + WFP), E3 egress mediator, E4 reference monitor. Classifiers, hooks, model self-report and content approvals are inputs to Π, never enforcement points. | WS-H4. |
| enforcement evidence | Per field group `{fs, net, proc, resources}`: `attested` (image/runtime identity verified) \| `reported` (helper asserted) \| `probed` (kernel self-test observed) \| `unknown`; never coerced; `unknown` ⇒ fail-closed for effects that rely on that group. | WS-H4. T-LCD-07 shape applied to enforcement; Codex `ProcessSandboxType` is `reported`. |
| containment report | `ContainmentReport{policy_version_id, backend, isolation_class, enforcement_evidence, lowering_loss[], probes[]}` returned by the helper at attach and re-validated on resume; the input the reference monitor's containment precondition reads. | WS-H4 / WS-B5 / WS-E5. |
| egress mediator | The E3 component on the host side of the boundary through which all network traffic of a `mediated` environment passes (bridged unix socket / loopback port / transparent redirect); decides `allow`/`deny` from policy, forwards `ask` to the monitor, resolves names, applies credential bindings, meters bytes, and emits one `security.egress.decided` per decision. | WS-H4. Codex `network-proxy`, sandbox-runtime proxies, Harbor egress sidecar. |
| egress decision | `EgressDecision{decision ∈ {allow, deny, ask}, source ∈ {mode_guard, unattributed, deny_rule, non_public_guard, protocol_guard, allow_rule, approval_cache, default_unmatched, monitor}, rule_ref?, reason, credential_binding_applied[]}` produced by `decide_egress` in a fixed evaluation order and keyed by `effect_id`. | WS-H4. Codex `NetworkDecisionSource`. |
| network mode | `net.mode ∈ {none (no namespace / no connect-class syscalls), mediated (namespace removed; only a bridged channel to the mediator), public (unmediated; principal-only; a declared residual)}`; proxy environment variables alone never constitute `mediated`. | WS-H4. Harbor `NetworkMode`, Inspect `network_mode: none`. |
| non-public destination guard | The mediator step that denies connections whose *resolved* address is loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, TEST-NET, reserved, unique-local, unspecified or multicast unless explicitly allow-listed; re-applied after name resolution. | WS-H4. Codex `policy.rs`/`connect_policy.rs`; SSRF prevention. |
| writable root / protected metadata name / KERNEL_PROTECTED | `WritableRoot{root, read_only_subpaths, protected_metadata_names}`; protected metadata names are paths under a writable root that stay read-only (VCS hooks, harness config/hook/skill/scheduled-task locations); `KERNEL_PROTECTED` is the kernel-supplied minimum no layer may remove. | WS-H4 / WS-H5. Codex `WritableRoot`; Claude Code protected paths; S-103 X-CPE write targets. |
| credential binding | The `EgressRule.credential_bindings: [CredentialRef]` slot naming which mediated credentials may be substituted for their sentinels on connections to this host; a sentinel bound to another host is forwarded unchanged (anti-laundering). Mechanism owned by WS-H3. | WS-H4 / WS-H3. sandbox-runtime `injectHosts`; Codex credential broker host binding. |
| containment amendment / escape hatch / strict mode | `amend(policy_version_id, diff, basis, endorser, effect_id?)`: the only run-time widening of containment; valid only with an endorser of class ≥ the loosened layer and a basis in `amendment.allowed_bases`; a model-issued "disable sandbox"/"allow host" parameter is a proposal converted to `ask` or ignored under `strict = true` (Lab default); every amendment is ledgered, budgeted and changes `configuration_version_id`. | WS-H4 / WS-H7. Claude Code `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`/`allowUnsandboxedCommands`; Codex escalation. |
| containment lowering loss report | The per-backend list `[LossItem{field, backend, reason}]` of policy fields the enforcement backend cannot enforce (e.g. unix sockets without a syscall filter; read restriction under a legacy filesystem backend; `chmod/chown` under Landlock); analogue of T-LCD-11 for containment; the Lab stratifies on it. | WS-H4 / WS-E5. |
| residual channel | `ResidualChannel{kind ∈ {approved_host_body, tls_opaque, dns_names, unix_socket, side_channel, host_bridge}, statement, closer, owner}` recorded on a policy for every exfiltration path the containment layer declares it does not close; an unowned residual fails readiness (T-LCD-05 shape). | WS-H4 / WS-H2. S-053 approved-domain exfiltration. |
| fail-closed (`ContainmentUnverified`) | The rule that a non-`read_only` effect is refused when the helper is unavailable, the backend unsupported, the report stale, or `enforcement_evidence = unknown` for a required field group; Lab runs always; interactive runs may declare `on_unavailable = warn_and_degrade`, stamped on every event and capping claims at R0. | WS-H4. Codex `enforce_managed_network` fail-closed; Claude Code `failIfUnavailable`. |
| attribution token | Opaque per-`(run_id, effect_id, attempt_no)` token minted by the executor and delivered to the child only through the bridged channel preface; the mediator maps it to the effect and denies unknown or mismatched tokens; unattributed connections are denied. | WS-H4 / WS-E5. Codex `CDXPXY1` attribution frame; sandbox-runtime `commandId`. |
